elevations.notes: Observed cream rusticated ground, three salmon/cream tall window rows, Corinthian upper piers, lower triangular pediments and low round-arched attic. Two axes on approximately 9m projecting source sections and the intervening regular modules are original section-fitted approximations, not an exact count surveyed over the entire 90m compound. Only one clearly observed wooden double portal is authored, near physical X-210m between source groups 10 and 8; its position/width are approximate, all other ground openings are glassshops. Unverified high gables above the lower source street-wall eave near Y14m retain neutral municipal source colour; curved corner/tower and roof/pavilion geometry remains unchanged.

limitations: Only the actually referenced public street elevation is restored. Other side walls, courtyards and roofs retain the municipal baseline.
Opening dimensions and module spacing are original authored approximations of the observed rhythm, not a measured architectural survey.
The ground profile is sampled from the pinned baseline HCOL and agrees with the rendered upward ground triangles; no ground or collision geometry is modified.

dimensions: Source plane bounds are exact municipal geometry; opening positions, dimensions and colours are authored approximations fitted to observed architectural rhythm. No survey accuracy is claimed.
